chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza and Al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Jameel and Ibn Bukayr,
regarding the child of a free man and a slave woman, he said: 'He goes to the free one from them'.
ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of a child born to a free man and a slave woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi articulates the foundational juristic principle of 'dhahab ila al-hurr' (going to the free), which resolves the status of offspring from a union between a free parent and an enslaved one. In Shia fiqh, this ruling ensures the child inherits the higher social and legal status of the free parent, facilitating their emancipation and integration into free society. The narration, transmitted through a chain of prominent Kufan scholars, underscores the practical application of this rule in determining lineage and freedom rights.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, and Al Hakam Bin Miskeen, from Jameel, and Ibn Bukeyr,
‘With regards to the child from the free man and the slave woman, he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would go to the free one from them’.
